key_insight: In epitaxial CsPbBr3 single crystals, terahertz and Hall measurements agree on the same intrinsic mobility, showing that defect-free charge transport can extend across millimetre scales.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical benchmark and validation method for separating intrinsic transport from defect-limited behavior in perovskite solar-cell materials.
method: Concurrent Hall-effect and optical pump–terahertz probe measurements on the same single-crystalline sample
Compare local ultrafast mobility with macroscopic steady-state transport mobility
Analyze temperature-dependent hole mobility to test for a shared band-like transport mechanism
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent room-temperature mobilities of about 30 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 from both Hall and terahertz methods, with similar temperature-power exponents.
watch_item: Results are shown for epitaxial CsPbBr3 single crystals, so extending the same intrinsic-transport behavior to polycrystalline films or device stacks may be limited by extrinsic disorder.
paper_title: Matching Terahertz and Hall Mobilities as a Hallmark of Intrinsic Charge Transport in Metal-Halide Perovskites
